title: Indian national missing after attacks on commercial vessel in Strait of Hormuz
author: PTI
content_html:
An Indian national went missing and two others sustained injuries after their Panama-flagged vessel came under attack in the Strait of Hormuz this week that triggered a strong condemnation from New Delhi.

The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said that of the 24 Indian nationals on board MT Tara Gas, 21 have been safely evacuated.

"We condemn the attack on the Panama-flagged LPG tanker MT Tara Gas in the Strait of Hormuz on 16 November 16," it said in a statement.

India said the targeting of commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure must end.

"Of the 24 Indian nationals on board, 21 have been safely evacuated ashore at Khasab, two injured Indian crew members have been admitted to hospital, while one Indian national remains missing," it added.

The MEA said the Embassy in Oman is closely monitoring the ongoing search and rescue operations in coordination with the Omani authorities.

"We appreciate the timely assistance and support extended by the Government of Oman in the rescue efforts," it said.

New Delhi said the "continuing incidents of attacks on shipping in the region are deeply worrisome and pose a serious threat to the safety of civilian seafarers."

"The targeting of commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure must end, and free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through international waterways, in keeping with international law, must be restored at the earliest," it said in a statement.

title: Nearly 75 lakh names added in draft SSR voters lists in 13 States and UTs
author: Sreeparna Chakrabarty
content_html:
Months after final voters lists were published following the contentious special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, nearly 75 lakh more names have been added in draft voter lists published in 13 States and Union Territories via a special summary revision process (SSR).

The combined size of the electorate in these States before the SIR was 49.61 crore, which shrunk to 45.22 crore after the SIR and has now increased to 45.96 crore in the draft SSR list. This means there has been a cumulative increase of 1.64 %.

Uttar Pradesh, which published its draft SSR list on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), saw 18.84 lakh names being added to its voter lists, the largest in absolute numbers so far. Goa saw the highest rate of additions, at 3.01 %. Bihar, which was the first State to undergo the SIR process in 2025 saw 13.89 lakh names being added to the final post-SIR list. Rajasthan saw more than 11.48 lakh voters being added to the final SIR voter list, followed by Uttarakhand (1.19 lakh), Madhya Pradesh (8.9 lakh), and Tamil Nadu (10.39 lakh).

No citizenship documents needed for SSR enrolment

The SSR, on hold since the SIR process began last year, was first announced in 17 States and UTs, including poll-bound Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, and Punjab, on October 15. On November 5, it was expanded to six more States where the SIR process is over, and on November 16, it was announced that the SSR would also be conducted in Karnataka and Meghalaya.

Of these, the draft SSR rolls have been published for 15 States and UTs. The data for Punjab and Gujarat, however, was not available.

The SSR, an annual exercise, usually seeks to enrol eligible voters, particularly young and first-time electors, and facilitate advance applications from those who will become eligible on April 1, July 1, and October 1, 2027. However, it had not been carried out after the SIR was launched last year, an anomaly that was recently highlighted by Election Commissioners S.S. Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.

Unlike the now contentious SIR process, when enrolling through the SSR, voters do not need to provide any documentation proving citizenship or be mapped with earlier electoral rolls.

Machine-readable voter lists

Among the firsts, in this year’s SSR, the ECI has directed that, at the time of the polls, a “readable PDF” of the alphabetically arranged electoral rolls can be provided to the contesting candidates in a pen drive or any other electronic storage device.

This is crucial as Opposition parties have been demanding machine-readable electoral rolls rather than image-based PDFs, so that they are digitally searchable, indexable, and verifiable. Political parties will also be provided with supplementary voter lists which were earlier kept only for records and future use.

The SSR process this time not only features the usual house-to-house visits by Booth Level Officers, but also includes the publication and display of draft as well as final voter lists at the polling booths.

title: Arguing that small and medium businesses and agriculture form the backbone of India's economy and are crucial for job creation, Rahul Gandhi said the country's manufacturing sector needed to be rebuilt
author: PTI
content_html:
India is sitting on an “economic disaster” with massive unemployment, a broken manufacturing base and deep-rooted problems in its education system, Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi said, warning that the country risks getting into serious trouble if it continues on the current economic path.

Speaking at a fireside chat at Columbia University in New York on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), the Congress leader said India's economic model "stopped giving results almost a decade ago" and criticised the government's initiatives such as 'Make in India' and 'Start-up India', claiming they had failed to revive the country's "broken" economic backbone.

"The blunt thing is that India is sitting on an economic disaster. That's the reality of it. One can brush it aside; the media can brush it aside. But India has got a massive unemployment problem. India's got a massive problem with its education system," he said.

Mr. Gandhi, who arrived in New York on Tuesday morning (November 17, 2026), was addressing hundreds of students and faculty members at the university.

Arguing that small and medium businesses and agriculture form the backbone of India's economy and are crucial for job creation, he said the country's manufacturing sector needed to be rebuilt.

"The spine of the economy is small and medium businesses, which are the job creation engine, and agriculture. That is fundamental in India and required," the politician said, adding that the "spine of the economy has been broken".

"You cannot give enough people jobs through services. It cannot be done. You can give 1%, 2%, 3%, 5%. You cannot give everybody a future with services. And we've just basically decided that we don't need manufacturing,” Mr. Gandhi said.

He questioned the lack of private investment and alleged that only a handful of large business groups, including those of Gautam Adani and Mukesh Ambani, were expanding, while smaller businesses were struggling.

“Why is there no private investment in India? Why are the only people who are growing in India, businesses that are growing in India, called Adani and Ambani? Why is Tata literally being taken over by Mr. Adani?”

Mr. Gandhi alleged that the economic architecture painstakingly built by the Congress party had been weakened and called for rebuilding it, saying India could not successfully develop without a strong manufacturing base.

"We cannot survive successfully without manufacturing; it just cannot be done," he said.

title: Fresh encounter in J&K’s Kulgam as security forces track escaped LeT terrorist Lateef Bhat
author: Peerzada Ashiq
content_html:
Security forces on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) killed LeT terrorist Lateef Bhat, who was hiding inside a mosque in south Kashmir’s Kulgam.

A team of security forces, who were tracking on-the-run Bhat, came under fire from inside a mosque around 3 a.m. in Kulgam’s Zangalpora. “We had a long conversation with him on the phone. We asked him to surrender but he refused. We exercised maximum restraint given he was hiding inside a mosque,” said Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Anayat Ali Choudhary.

“It’s a big success, given the fact he joined (the terror outfit) in November last year. He was radicalised and would take guidelines from across to hit peace, tourism and economy here (Kashmir),” said SSP Choudhary.

Senior officials said Bhat, 22, was later killed in the joint operation of the Army and the J&K Police.

Bhat attacked CRPF personnel in Kulgam’s Akhran area on November 11, which left three jawans injured. In the past eight days, security forces continued multiple anti-terror operations in the district and killed Bhat’s accomplice Umar Nisar Dar, a baker by profession, two days ago in Kulgam’s Laroo Bypass area.

According to the police, both Bhat and Dar were behind the November 11 attack in Kulgam. Bhat was also behind the twin attacks in Anantnag and Kulgam, which left one policeman and two non-local labourers from Chhattisgarh dead in July this year. The J&K Police had announced a cash reward of ₹15 lakh on him.

Bhat was a resident of Khrewan Chader in Kulgam’s Ashmuji and would work as a carpenter.

Meanwhile, an Army spokesman said security forces displayed exemplary restraint during the conduct of operations “ensuring the sanctity of the religious place and neutralised the terrorist with precision by forcing him to move out of the mosque premises”. “The operation is in progress,” said the Army.

title: Cyclone 'Akvan' LIVE updates: Likely to intensify into severe cyclonic storm today, IMD says
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Key Updates
  • Watch: All you need to know about Cyclone Akvan
  • Cyclone Akvan: 540 km of Andhra and Yanam coast braces for November 20 landfall

  • November 18, 2026 12:30
    Akvan may cross between Machilipatnam and Puri: APSDMA

    Cyclone Akvan is now likely to cross the coast between Machilipatnam and Puri, along the north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts, around noon on Friday (November 20) as a severe cyclonic storm, the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) said in an update at 12.10 p.m. on Wednesday.

    The storm picked up speed to 7 kmph over the past six hours. It was about 580 km from Visakhapatnam, 590 km from Machilipatnam and 710 km from Gopalpur in Odisha, APSDMA said.

    The authority asked people in the north coastal districts to stay alert. -- The Hindu Bureau

  • November 18, 2026 12:23
    Latest update from IMD on Cyclone Akvan

    The Severe Cyclonic Storm “Akvan” over central parts of South and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal moved north-northwestwards with the speed of 07 kmph during past 06 hours and lay centered at 0830 hours IST on November 18, 2026 over the same region, near Latitude 12.9°N and Longitude 85.4°E, about 570 km east of Chennai (Tamil Nadu), 580 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 590 km southeast of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 660 km northeast of Trincomalee (Sri Lanka), 710 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha) and 770 km south of Puri (Odisha).

    Continuing to move north-northwestward, it is likely to cross North Andhra Pradesh & Yanam and South Odisha coasts between Machilipatnam and Puri, by noon of 20th November, 2026 as a severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph.

    Akvan.jpg

  • November 18, 2026 11:44
    Odisha restricts beach tourism, coastal recreation ahead of Cyclone Akvon’s landfall in Andhra

    The Odisha government has restricted coastal tourism activities and beach recreation as the Bay of Bengal turned choppy ahead of Cyclone Akvan’s expected landfall in neighbouring Andhra Pradesh on India’s east coast on Friday (November 20, 2026).

    The India Meteorological Department said the severe cyclonic storm with maximum sustained wind speed of 100-110 kmph and gusting up to 120 kmph was likely to cross Andhra Pradesh between Nellore and Visakhapatnam around noon on November 20.

    It is likely to whip up a storm in Odisha with wind speed reaching 40-50 kmph on Thursday and increasing to 50-60 kmph the next day and the day after. The sea would remain rough from the night of November 18 to 21, the weather department said.

    In the wake of the weather warning, Odisha’s Special Relief Commissioner (SRC) Rajesh P Patil wrote to commissioner cum secretary of the tourism department to ensure enforcement of safety measures immediately.

    “There is an urgent need to safeguard tourists, visitors, tourism personnel and the general public from risks arising from rough seas, strong winds, heavy rainfall and coastal inundation,” the SRC mentioned in the letter. -- PTI

  • November 18, 2026 11:39
    Telangana puts four districts on orange alert

    IMD Hyderabad Meteorologist GNRS Srinivas said Cyclone Akvan is likely to affect Telangana after crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast, with four eastern districts placed under an orange alert for November 20.

    Speaking in Hyderabad, Srinivas said the cyclone, which formed over the southeast Bay of Bengal three days ago, had intensified into a cyclone by the previous evening and was likely to strengthen further into a severe cyclone over the West Central Bay of Bengal by Tuesday evening or night.

    He said the system was likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Thune on the morning or afternoon of November 20, and its effects could also be felt in Telangana.

    “Some of the eastern districts in Telangana are put under orange alert on the 20th. These districts are Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Mahabubabad, and Suryapet... By tomorrow evening, the picture will be clearer. And accordingly, the forecast for Telangana can be modified...” he said.

    Srinivas said the weather forecast for Telangana could be revised as the cyclone’s movement and intensity become clearer. -- ANI

  • November 18, 2026 11:38
    Odisha turns focus to landslides in hills as Cyclone Akvan approaches

    The Odisha government is planning to shift over 2 lakh people from vulnerable areas, particularly landslide-prone hilly regions, as Cyclone Akvan approaches the coast ahead of its expected landfall in neighbouring Andhra Pradesh on Friday (November 20, 2026), officials said.

    The preparedness measures were finalised on Tuesday at a review meeting chaired by Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari, who said landslides had emerged as a major challenge for the state, which already had established mechanisms to deal with floods and cyclones.

    Of the 11 deaths reported during last month’s cyclone Arnab, 10 were caused by landslides, Pujari said, adding that the government was taking precautions to shift people living in foothill areas and hilltop hamlets across southern Odisha.

    Six districts, Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Kandhamal, Malkangiri and Koraput, have been identified as highly vulnerable to landslides, officials said.

    The Special Relief Commissioner’s (SRC) office has asked the Odisha Remote Sensing Application Centre (ORSAC) to provide satellite imagery and GIS-based maps of landslide-prone villages and road stretches in these districts. -- PTI

  • November 18, 2026 11:36
    NDRF, SDRF teams kept ready for emergency operations: Anitha

    Home Minister V Anitha has said that 13 NDRF teams, 11 SDRF teams, and fire service units have been kept ready for emergency relief operations arising out of Cyclone Akvan.

    Ms Anitha, who reviewed the preparedness with officials on Wednesday, had directed the state machinery to remain on a high alert for the next 48 hours. She asked officials to take all possible measures to prevent loss of life and property. She said heavy to very heavy rainfall is expected in the coastal districts for the next two days starting November 19.

    Ms Anitha advised the public to remain vigilant and urged people living in coastal areas to avoid stepping out unless absolutely necessary. She asked people living in low-lying areas to move to relief centers as and when instructed by the authorities.

    Meanwhile, Energy Minister Gottipati Ravikumar reviewed preparedness for Cyclone Aqvan with electricity department and asked them to remain on high alert across the region from Nellore to Visakhapatnam. -- Hareesh P.

    According to a 8.30 a.m. bulletin from the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the system was located at 5.30 a.m. at about 580 km east of Chennai of Tamil Nadu, 650 km northeast of Trincomalee of Sri Lanka, 610 km southeast of Machilipatnam of Andhra Pradesh, 610 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam of Andhra Pradesh and 730 km south of Gopalpur of Odisha.

title: Nepal gets nod to import 350 MW of power from India during winter
author: PTI
content_html:
Nepal has received approval to import up to 350 MW of electricity from India this winter to meet domestic power demand amid a decline in hydropower generation and damage to several projects caused by recent floods.

The Central Electricity Authority (CEA) under India's Ministry of Power has authorised the Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA), the State-owned power utility, to procure electricity at competitive rates from the Indian Energy Exchange (IEX) for up to 17 hours a day, NEA officials said.

The approval is valid from November 17, 2026, to July 31, 2027, and is expected to help Nepal manage the seasonal gap between electricity demand and domestic generation, NEA Managing Director Dirghayu Kumar Shrestha said.

Of the approved 350 MW, Nepal can import 300 MW through the Kataiya-Kushaha, Ramnagar-Surajpura and Raxaul-Parwanipur transmission lines. The remaining 50 MW can be sourced through the New Nautanwa-Mainahiya transmission line.

Nepal's dependence on run-of-the-river hydropower projects makes electricity generation highly seasonal.

While rising river flows during the summer months enable the country to generate surplus power for export, mainly to India, declining water levels during winter significantly reduce domestic production, forcing it to rely on imports.

The country's power supply situation has also been affected by the damage caused to several hydropower projects in central Nepal during the devastating Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi floods in August.

Projects with a combined installed capacity of 431 MW have remained disconnected from the national grid following the disaster.

However, domestic generation is expected to improve from mid-April as water levels in rivers gradually rise, reducing Nepal's dependence on imported electricity and potentially allowing it to resume exports, officials said.

title: Jharkhand BJP delegation meets Governor, seeks Congress MLA’s arrest in assault case
author: Amit Bhelari
content_html:
The Jharkhand unit of the Bharatiya Janata Party’s Scheduled Tribe Morcha, led by Sunny Toppo, met Governor Santosh Gangwar on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) and submitted a memorandum to him over “rising crimes against women, particularly tribals” in the State.

Highlighting the allegation that Congress’s Simdega MLA Bhushan Bara raped a 14-year-old girl, the Opposition party questioned why no arrest has been made despite the registration of an FIR.

The National Commission for Women and the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes have also sought reports on the issue from the Jharkhand government. The Congress is a constituent of the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha-led ruling coalition.

On November 14, hours after the FIR was registered against Mr. Bara, the police said they had booked two persons, based on a complaint by the girl’s grandfather, for allegedly abducting and coercing the girl into making a “false” statement against the two-time legislator. Leader of the Opposition in the Assembly Babulal Marandi alleged that one of those booked is a journalist.

The Opposition party has sought to corner the Hemant Soren-led government over a series of crimes, which include the Simdega incident, a sexual assault in Hotwar jail and the alleged rape of a woman who had gone to the Gamharia police station seeking justice. Fifteen police officers were suspended in connection with the Gamharia incident on November 1.

The delegation led by Mr. Toppo also called for an impartial probe into the recent death of tribal leader Nisha Kumari Bhagat.

During the day, BJP members staged a demonstration outside Lok Bhavan in Ranchi, demanding the immediate arrest of Mr. Bara. “We are protesting against the sexual exploitation of a 14-year-old tribal girl. The victim has shown great courage by lodging an FIR against the MLA. Instead of properly investigating the matter, action is being taken against a journalist who exposed it,” said senior BJP leader and former MP Geeta Koda.

(With inputs from PTI)
